Question: When is illegal recruitment considered an offense involving economic sabotage?
Expected Answer: When it is committed by a syndicate or in large scale. It is committed by a syndicate when it is carried out by a group of three (3) or more persons conspiring or confederating with one another. It is committed in large scale when it is committed against three (3) or more persons, individually or as a group.

Check Phrase(s): considered as offense involving economic sabotage
Look-alike Passages: p1-s2-par1 (B-3) — the definition says offering jobs for a fee to “two or more persons” counts as recruitment; that number is not the economic-sabotage rule
Why This Difficulty: The answer needs two conditions plus what “syndicate” and “large scale” mean, read together from the passage.
Evidence Passages (verbatim): [p2-s2-par3] Illegal recruitment when committed by a syndicate or in large scale shall be considered as offense involving economic sabotage. It is deemed committed in large scale if committed against three (3) or more persons individually or as a group.

Question: What is a No Objection Certification (NOC) for Special Recruitment Authority, and who may avail of it?
Expected Answer: It is a clearance issued by the DMW (or the DOLE Regional/Field Office) to a licensed recruitment agency. It shows that the government has no objection to the agency recruiting outside its registered business address for Special Recruitment Activities. The Local Government Unit (LGU) or Pre-Employment Service Office often requires it before the agency can set up at a local venue such as a municipal hall or gym. Only licensed recruitment agencies may avail of it, and the Total Standard Fee is None.
